title: KOL strategies: what well-known Solana memecoin traders say about how they trade
summary: Public trading habits of well-known Solana memecoin traders (KOLs), summarised in plain words from their own dated posts: style, entries, exits, sizing, what you can learn, and what not to copy.
label: Public opinions, not verified track records, not advice.
intro: KOL means key opinion leader: a trader with a big public following. This page collects what a few of them have said in public about how they trade, written in our own words, with links to the dated posts we read.
We do not verify anyone's profits. Wallets can be split, borrowed, or shown selectively, and leaderboards can be gamed. Treat every entry as one person's public opinion about their own process.
how_chosen: Four featured traders were chosen by us: cupsey, frankdegods, unipcs and pointfarmcap. Every handle was checked against X's user lookup on Oct 27, 2026. The unipcs X handle is @theunipcs.

The other five are FOMO traders. FOMO (fomo.family) is a social trading app with public PnL leaderboards for 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days and all time. Those rankings change every day and there is no single official list we could verify, so we used three filters: (1) the trader appeared on a public FOMO ranking snapshot (FomoRadar's 30-day Solana list or Provadata's 7-day leaderboard, both read Oct 26-27, 2026) or in FOMO's own trader-spotlight posts on X (September-October 2026); (2) not already one of the four names above; (3) a public, unprotected X account with posts about how they trade. Accounts that were protected, suspended or could not be matched to an X handle were dropped.

Leaderboards can be gamed. One FOMO trader warned in public that scam tokens (honeypots or tokens with freeze authority) can inflate a wallet's paper PnL, which is one more reason not to treat rank as skill.

traders.name: Cupsey
traders.who: A full-time Solana 'trenches' trader known for fast trading of fresh launches.
traders.style: High-volume, short-hold trading of new coins, with long screen sessions.

habits.entry: Has said quality beats quantity: spend more time on a few coins rather than buying lots of them.
habits.exit: Known for quick trades on new coins, but has also said that sitting on your hands with a coin you believe in is how the biggest gains come.
habits.size: No public sizing rule found in the posts we read.

learn: Fewer, better-researched trades beat spraying buys across many coins.
Review your trades. He has talked about running a trading-journal group to reflect on trades, with no calls posted.

Wallet security is part of trading: he said in Sept 2025 that a wallet connected to several trading apps was drained for about $500,000 overnight. Use a separate hot wallet that holds only what you trade with.
dont_copy: 16-hour 'trench shifts'. That speed and screen time is his job, not a plan for a normal trader.
Connecting a large wallet to many apps.

traders.name: Frank (frankdegods)
traders.who: A well-known onchain and perps trader with one of the largest followings in Solana trading.
traders.style: Short, event-driven trades: each buy has a specific reason, and he cuts it quickly when the reason does not play out.

habits.entry: In an Aug 2026 reply he listed a run of trades, each with a one-line reason: news about to spread, a launch on a new launchpad, a livestream that might bring an announcement.
habits.exit: The same list shows the exit rule: if the expected event does not happen, or he realises he is late and it is priced in, he cuts. Some were held for a week, some for 30 seconds.
habits.size: Has said most trading problems come from being a forced seller: if you have to sell one coin to buy another, your size is the problem.

learn: Write the reason for every trade and the condition that ends it.
Size so you never have to sell a good position just to free up cash.
Coins that need paid promoters tend to have lower ceilings, because the promoters sell and move on.
Be honest about results. He posted on Oct 24, 2026 that he is not up overall on his main perps wallet and most of his money has come from onchain trading.
dont_copy: 30-second flips on brand-new launchpads. That needs speed and tools most people do not have.
Trading off news flow you only see after it has spread.
traders.stat: An OnchainLens post on Oct 24, 2026 said FOMO's all-time PnL leaderboard showed frankdegods at about +$3.13M, second behind Unipcs. That is a third-party snapshot, not a verified record.

traders.name: Unipcs ('Bonk Guy')
traders.who: A Solana memecoin trader best known for holding BONK early and for big conviction holds.
traders.style: Conviction holding. He says his edge is not being early but holding winners for a long time.

habits.entry: Says he often finds winners late, is usually not among the first buyers, and has bought coins above a $5M market cap.
habits.exit: Holds with conviction. He has also said he round-tripped more than $20M on BONK out of loyalty, so holding has a cost.
habits.size: In Oct 2026 he wrote about losing about $100K on a rug after overtrading new pairs and oversizing on what he called borrowed conviction.

learn: You do not need to be first. A strong coin can still be bought after it has proven itself.
Sometimes the best trade is no trade, especially after a loss.
Do not blindly copytrade anyone: he says about 90% of tokens sent to his FOMO wallet are airdrops meant to bait copytraders, and he sells them.
Decide in advance how much of a big gain you are willing to give back.
dont_copy: Holding through very deep drawdowns. He has posted about a large drop from a portfolio peak; that only works with money and nerves most people do not have.
Copytrading his wallet. In his words, copytrade him at your own risk.
traders.stat: An OnchainLens post on Oct 24, 2026 said he was #1 on FOMO's all-time PnL leaderboard at about +$3.20M. Third-party snapshot, not verified.

traders.name: Point Farm Capital
traders.who: A trader known for Hyperliquid, points farming and perps, now also active trading memecoins on FOMO.
traders.style: Opinionated on narratives: favours simple memes and under-watched coins and ecosystems.

habits.entry: Looks for coins and ecosystems that lack attention yet. Has said that if you have to explain the meme, you have already lost.
habits.exit: Has said borrowed conviction does not last: if you hold only because someone else is bullish, you will sell at the worst time.
habits.size: No public sizing rule found in the posts we read.

learn: If you cannot explain why a meme is funny or viral in one sentence, skip it.
Open positions on your own conviction, not someone else's.
Read people's reasons, not just their buys: he has said FOMO's thesis section (traders' written reasons) is useful.
dont_copy: His perps and points background gives him tools and context a beginner lacks.
Ranking spikes. A 7-day leaderboard rank can change by the next week.
traders.stat: He was #1 on Provadata's FOMO 7-day leaderboard when we read it on Oct 27, 2026 (00:38 IST). Weekly ranks change constantly.

traders.name: Steven (bystevenr)
traders.fomo_basis: #2 on FomoRadar's 30-day Solana list; FOMO posted an interview with him on Oct 12, 2026.
traders.who: A swing trader who trades across assets, including Solana memecoins.
traders.style: Patient swing longs he calls 'delayed gratification' setups.

habits.entry: Buys swing setups and waits; has described watching money flow off pump.fun to other launchpads and then rotate back.
habits.exit: Sets a wide invalidation level in advance (he mentioned 40% on a swing long) and holds until it is hit or the idea plays out.
habits.size: Has described a barbell: a defensive position elsewhere and memecoin trades with limited downside.

learn: Decide where you are wrong before you buy, and size so that level is affordable.
Watch where liquidity is moving between launchpads.
Take your own trades. He has told followers exactly that.
dont_copy: A 40% invalidation with large size. A wide stop only works with a small position.
Cross-asset hedging, unless you understand the other side of the barbell.

traders.name: Q (Quanterty)
traders.fomo_basis: Featured in FOMO's trader spotlight on X on Oct 18, 2026.
traders.style: Large, aggressive positions, and unusually open about his own mistakes.

habits.entry: Has talked about keeping cash ready to buy a pullback instead of being fully invested.
habits.exit: Has said his biggest problem is not selling when he is up big, then round-tripping. He also wrote about cancelling a take-profit order and regretting it.
habits.size: Has blamed 'stupid sizing' for giving back gains.

learn: Triple-check every order before you send it: he said one mistyped sell order cost him about $100K.
Put take-profits in and leave them alone.
Keep some cash for pullbacks.
Take breaks. He has stepped back for his mental health.
dont_copy: His position sizes and risk appetite.
Cancelling planned exits when a coin is running.

traders.name: kanye south (pedrigavifrenki)
traders.fomo_basis: Featured in FOMO's trader spotlight on X on Oct 6, 2026 ('on-chain narratives, held with conviction').
traders.who: A trader of onchain narratives who holds positions with conviction.
traders.style: Narrative trades, checked onchain, held while the story keeps growing.

habits.entry: Tracks large wallets to see where money is going, and checks slippage and whether a token can actually be sold (honeypot check) before buying.
habits.exit: Holds while the narrative is alive.
habits.size: Says he will never go all in again after a past position fell from about $1.3M unrealized to about $300K in May 2022.

learn: Never go all in on one coin.
Check you can sell before you buy.
Use wallet tracking as research, not as a copy button.
dont_copy: Conviction holds without a plan for how much you will give back.

traders.name: heat
traders.fomo_basis: #5 on FomoRadar's 30-day Solana list. He posted on Oct 26, 2026 that he was #1 over 24 hours and #3 over 30 days. We matched the FOMO name to this X account from his bio and posts; that match is likely, but not confirmed. His bio warns about impersonators.
traders.who: A Solana memecoin trader active on FOMO.
traders.style: High-conviction bets that he openly calls a gamble, judged on risk/reward.

habits.entry: His recent posts describe buying a healthy pullback after a pump, on the main runner of a launchpad, rather than the first spike.
habits.exit: No public exit rule found in the posts we read.
habits.size: No public sizing rule found in the posts we read.

learn: Buy the pullback on the strongest coin, not the first green candle.
Call a gamble a gamble and size it like one.
dont_copy: Any coin he names. Several of his posts include contract addresses; copying a KOL's coin after they post it often means buying their exit.

traders.name: k4rl (kv4rl)
traders.fomo_basis: #3 on Provadata's FOMO 7-day leaderboard when read on Oct 27, 2026.
traders.who: A Solana memecoin trader whose bio is about 'increasing luck surface area'.
traders.style: Contrarian: buys when the outcome is uncertain and sells when everyone is sure.

habits.exit: Sells into certainty, when the story is obvious to everyone.
habits.size: No public sizing rule found in the posts we read.

learn: The crowd being sure is often the time to sell, not buy.
Scrolling crypto X is the fastest way to get shaken out of good positions. Decide your plan off-screen.
If you do not believe in a coin, do not hold it.
dont_copy: Contrarian bets without a stop. Uncertainty means many of them go to zero.

common.title: What these traders agree on
items: Your own conviction beats borrowed conviction. Holding a coin only because a KOL holds it ends with you selling at the bottom.
Copytrading a public wallet is risky: wallets get baited with airdrops, and you are always later than the trader.
Size is the most common cause of big losses they describe: oversizing, going all in, or being forced to sell.
Giving back gains (round-tripping) is the most common regret. Plan your take-profits and keep them.
Taking breaks, journaling and sometimes not trading at all are part of the job.

add_more: This section is data-driven. More traders will be added over time, in the same format.
closing: Not financial advice. No strategy wins every trade, and you can lose everything in memecoins. Nothing here is a call to buy any coin or to copy any wallet.
